object_description: simple compact volume occupying the terrace edge, three to four storeys depending on the slope
geometry_property: three to four storeys depending on position
inner courtyard up to the ground floor
concrete element facade with OSB infills
design_condition: the compact volume occupies the edge of the terrace and clearly defines the prominent location on the slope, with the double gymnasium placed in the basement to keep it compact

positive: A simple and compact building volume was developed in urban planning terms
The volume occupies the edge of the terrace and clearly defines the prominent slope location
Compactness is made possible by placing the double gymnasium in the basement
Outdoor facilities are organised in terraces around the building
The simple structure was attractively designed and structured
Concrete element facades with infills structure the building in a simple way
The inner courtyard reaching the ground floor provides a pleasant lighting atmosphere in the access area
The visible wooden construction inside is surprising
The compact volumetry detached from the neighbouring street is well proportioned in the terrain
A spacious break area is divided into different areas with diverse, child-suitable uses
The grass playing field nestles between school and housing, creating a pleasant distance
The connection to the neighbourhood is good and the routing is plausible
The interior organisation largely corresponds to the idea of the school from the ground floor up
The compact plans allow the primary school to be clearly organised over just a few floors
A naturally designed learning landscape develops with well-lit classrooms and group rooms
Furnishable corridor situations sit at the inner courtyard
Economic efficiency and sustainability requirements are well met from the ground floor up
negative: Placing the gymnasium in the basement leads to significant degradation of the rock in the subsoil
The infill elements cannot really improve the overall impression of the facade
The connection to the terrain is not yet convincingly solved structurally in all places
Whether the concrete element facade suits the wooden construction inside is questionable
The all-weather pitch is somewhat out of place in the landscape
Fire protection on the upper floors is not adequately addressed
Escape routes from the group rooms do not lead directly into the escape corridor
The stairwells do not lead directly outdoors
The basement sports hall generates a very uneven lighting situation when divided
The significant rock erosion for the gymnasium is considered detrimental
